name: WABOT-2
def: Keyboard playing humanoid from Waseda University that read printed sheet music with a camera eye and performed on an electronic organ.
body: WABOT-2 was built as a specialist musician rather than a general purpose machine, with ten fingers, two feet and about fifty joints. A camera in its head read ordinary sheet music, and a distributed network of roughly eighty microprocessors coordinated fingers, feet and speech so it could play organ pieces of moderate difficulty and accompany a singer. It performed in public at Expo '85 in Tsukuba.
facts: Read printed scores and played an electronic organ
specs: About 50 joints driven by electric motors
Camera eye for reading printed scores, microphone
